clue.text: Salt is wholesome

definitions.meaning: an old salt is a seasoned sailor, and sailors hail each other as shipmates in this way
nourishing and healthy, as a substantial meal is

explanation.definitionFit: A sailor is addressed as 'me hearty' in sea talk, and a robust, nourishing meal is called hearty.

clue.text: Help member of crew to get bag

parts.note: a hand is a worker, especially a sailor in a ship's crew
a grip is an old word for a travelling bag or holdall

explanation.surface: Someone asks for assistance so that one of the crew can fetch their luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something to grasp gives support to anyone climbing or steadying themselves, so it serves as an aid.

clue.text: Out of place, a friend is cut off

indicators.note: the friend's word lies outside, with the word for place coming out of its middle

parts.note: a mate is a pal or friend
to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: Someone feels displaced and estranged after a friend is shut out of their life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of place' reads as one phrase meaning awkward, but 'Out of' is the container signal and 'place' gives PUT, set inside MATE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove a limb surgically is to sever it from the body.

clue.text: Craftsman once more fired up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
lit means set alight, fired

explanation.surface: An old tradesman has had his kiln lit again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RELIT (RE plus LIT) to read from the bottom of the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofer or bathroom fitter who lays ceramic squares is a skilled tradesperson.

clue.text: Taking part in exchange in South London area

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
Wapping is a district of East London by the Thames

explanation.surface: Someone joins a swap meet in a part of south London.
explanation.walkthrough: WAPPING is a riverside district of East London, once home to many newspaper printworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading one thing for another is participating in a barter.

clue.text: Fighting war bolstered winners ultimately

indicators.note: fighting suggests the letters are in turmoil, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An army made stronger for the battle ends up victorious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighting' scrambles the twelve letters of WAR BOLSTERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who outdo everyone on the planet are champions of the highest order.

clue.text: One is given double quantity of ecstasy south of here

indicators.note: in a down light, below means the following piece comes after

parts.note: present means here, in attendance

indicators.note: a double quantity asks for the letter to be written twice

parts.note: E is slang shorthand for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A clubber is handed twice the usual dose of drugs down the road from here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double quantity of' gives EE, which 'south of' places below PRESENT in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipient of a gift, someone to whom something is handed, is so called.

clue.text: Woman at home keeps cat safe at last

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: in means at home, not out
mog or moggy is British slang for a cat

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A woman indoors keeps her cat secure in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts MOG plus E (the last letter of 'safe') inside IN; MOG is British slang for a house cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Imogen is a girl's name, borne by the heroine of Shakespeare's Cymbeline.

clue.text: Thick oily substance forming film

definitions.meaning: a lubricant such as axle fat
a 1978 musical film starring John Travolta and Olivia Newton-John

explanation.definitionFit: Lubricating fat is the common noun, and the 1978 high-school musical movie bears the same title.

clue.text: Foreign language, one used by the French writer on reflection

indicators.note: reflection as in a mirror means the letters of the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
la is the feminine form of the in French
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A French author mulls over a foreign tongue he has picked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns the whole run ILAPEN to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepali is the national tongue of Nepal, spoken in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Final remains of corpse in morgue's terribly ---

definitions.text: Final remains of corpse in morgue's terribly ---

indicators.note: in places the single letter within the scrambled letters
terribly suggests the letters are badly messed up, signalling a rearrangement
the final remaining letter of the word that follows is taken

explanation.surface: The last vestiges of a body in the mortuary are horribly grisly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' scrambles MORGUES (the 's counted as a letter) and 'in' puts E, the last letter of 'corpse', among them. The dash invites the solver to finish the sentence with the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A decaying body left in a mortuary is a horrible, ghastly sight, which the whole clue depicts.

clue.text: Artiste much exercised about English entertainment

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the next piece
exercised suggests the letters are worked over and moved about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer gets very worked up over an English show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercised' rearranges ARTISTE MUCH, and 'about' wraps those letters round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage musicals are a genre of popular show business.

clue.text: Be socially active: buy everyone a drink

definitions.meaning: to go out a lot and mix with many people
to stand a round at the bar, paying for the whole group

explanation.definitionFit: A busy social life means circulating widely, and a pub round is one person paying for every glass in the party.

clue.text: Water carriers used by brewer systematically

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A brewery methodically uses its jugs to carry water.
explanation.definitionFit: Large jugs or pitchers hold and pour water.

clue.text: Clever fellow on popular TV broadcast

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the fellow comes after the other piece
broadcast means spoken out, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: popular means in, and TV is the telly, giving in telly
gent is short for gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A bright man appears on a well-loved television show.
explanation.walkthrough: IN TELLY (popular TV) is heard as INTELLI, and 'on' puts GENT after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright and quick-witted, with a sharp mind.

clue.text: Form of transport: get off and complain

parts.note: to light, or alight, is to get off a vehicle
to rail against something is to complain bitterly

explanation.surface: A commuter climbs down from a train and grumbles about the service.
explanation.definitionFit: Tram and metro systems running on tracks are a kind of urban passenger service.

clue.text: Mrs Simpson gets in a state over a get-together

indicators.note: gets in means the next letters are taken inside the name

parts.note: Marge Simpson is the mother in the cartoon series The Simpsons

indicators.note: in a down light, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for the US state Rhode Island

explanation.surface: Marge Simpson gets agitated over a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' is a misleading phrase for flustered; 'state' gives RI, placed 'over' A, and 'gets in' puts RIA inside MARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding unites two people, a union or coming together.

clue.text: Film star as a boy visiting Mexico, for instance

indicators.note: visiting means calling in, so the boy goes inside

parts.note: Mexico is an example of a country or land
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: An actor once started out as a youngster on a trip to Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visiting' puts LAD inside LAND, after A. Alan Ladd was a Hollywood actor famous for the western Shane.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Ladd was a 1940s and 1950s Hollywood leading man.

clue.text: Fail to follow part of tourist itinerary in China

definitions.meaning: to collapse in ruin, as a failing business does

definitions.text: follow part of tourist itinerary in China
definitions.meaning: visitors to China make a trip to the Great Wall

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a business is ruined, and literally it is a tourist's trip to the Great Wall of China.

clue.text: Charitable woman supplying some food or cash

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A kindly woman hands out a little food or money.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'supplying' in the definition, but it is a link word: 'Charitable woman' alone defines, and 'supplying' joins it to the hidden run. Dorcas, in Acts, was famed for her good works.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorcas, also called Tabitha, is the New Testament woman known for her alms and good deeds.

clue.text: Saint tucks into fruit for religious festival

indicators.note: tucks into means goes inside, so the letter sits within the fruit

parts.note: a peach is a fruit

explanation.surface: A holy man eats some fruit at a sacred feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' looks like eating, but it puts S inside PEACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesach is the Hebrew name for Passover, the Jewish spring festival.

clue.text: Check time by old Olympic runner

indicators.note: by means next to, so the letter for old sits beside the other pieces

parts.note: to vet something is to check it

explanation.surface: An official checks the clock beside a veteran runner.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Ovett is the British middle-distance runner who won Olympic 800m gold in 1980.
explanation.definitionFit: Steve Ovett is a British athlete who won gold at the Moscow Games.

clue.text: Settled near Loire beforehand

indicators.note: settled suggests the letters come to rest in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone moved to a place close to the French river some time ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Previously, at a prior point in time.

clue.text: Current charge will get you steamed up

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: Being billed for electricity leaves a customer fuming.
explanation.definitionFit: Angry and agitated, hot under the collar.

clue.text: Man cut Greek bread

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: Attic means of ancient Athens, Greek

explanation.surface: A man slices Greek loaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like slicing, but it trims the C from ATTIC to leave ATTI.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapatti is an unleavened flatbread from South Asia.

clue.text: First to hire a vehicle near a foreign capital

indicators.note: first to picks the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A traveller hires a van as soon as they reach a capital abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Havana is the capital city of Cuba.

clue.text: German writer's second book of horror

definitions.note: the 's is read as is, linking the writer to the wordplay

parts.note: a chiller is a frightening story

explanation.surface: A German author's second novel is a horror story.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Schiller was a German poet and dramatist, author of William Tell.

clue.text: Top male in a bit of a sweat

indicators.note: in means the male pronoun goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a bead is a drop of sweat
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: The head man gets into a lather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like a noun or adjective but is the verb, to execute.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is slang for executing them, cutting off the head.
